thesis: Abercrombie disclosed record fiscal-Q2 sales of $1.267 billion, 5% year-over-year growth, and raised full-year sales and GAAP diluted-EPS outlook after both brands grew. The strongest counter-evidence is that comparable sales were flat, Hollister comparable sales fell 3%, and $1.75 of the quarter's $4.17 GAAP diluted EPS came from tariff refunds; that tempers the quality of the jump but does not erase the continuing top-line growth, higher outlook, and share reduction. The late-October trial of former CEO Michael Jeffries and related company civil actions add material event and governance risk, so the net read supports a long thesis only at low conviction.
invalidation: Comparable sales turn negative across both brands, tariff-refund benefits fail to translate into durable operating performance, or management lowers the newly raised fiscal-2026 sales or earnings outlook.

thesis: Biohaven disclosed a signed global licensing agreement that provides $350 million at closing and another $50 million in 2027, up to $150 million of additional development and regulatory milestones, royalties, and transfer of specified Kv7 obligations to SK Biopharmaceuticals. The strongest counter-evidence is that closing remains subject to antitrust and customary conditions and both the milestones and opakalim's Phase 2/3 outcome remain uncertain; this does not change the read because the signed deal itself supplies substantial non-dilutive near-term capital and shifts future program costs to an experienced epilepsy partner. The targeted checks found active litigation but no scheduled adverse company or executive hearing, ruling, trial, or compliance deadline in the next roughly 90 days, and no qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: The transaction fails its closing conditions, the near-term cash consideration is materially delayed or reduced, or RISE3 data undermine opakalim's efficacy or tolerability premise.

thesis: KANZHUN disclosed fiscal-Q2 revenue growth of 14.1%, GAAP operating-income growth of 32.6%, 10.8% growth in paid enterprise customers, and record average monthly active users. The strongest counter-evidence is that the 173.1% GAAP net-income increase was dominated by a fair-value investment gain, while adjusted non-GAAP net income grew only 9.4% and operating cash flow fell 10.2%; this does not change the core read because customer, revenue, and GAAP operating-income growth all strengthened without relying on that investment gain. Targeted litigation and governance checks found no qualifying scheduled event in the next roughly 90 days and no qualifying restatement, for-cause auditor departure, or operations-related indictment or plea in the last three years.
invalidation: Paid-customer or revenue growth decelerates sharply, GAAP operating-income growth reverses, or regulatory changes materially impair the recruitment platform's operation or U.S. listing.

thesis: Semtech disclosed record fiscal-Q2 net sales of $341.9 million, up 33% year over year, GAAP operating margin of 16.3%, adjusted non-GAAP operating margin of 24.4%, and a materially higher non-GAAP fiscal-Q3 sales and margin outlook. The strongest counter-evidence is that a $101.4 million GAAP tax benefit inflated GAAP net income and diluted EPS, and the stronger fiscal-Q3 outlook remains forward-looking; this does not change the read because record revenue and the expansion in both GAAP operating margin and adjusted non-GAAP operating margin demonstrate operating improvement before that tax benefit. Targeted litigation and governance checks found no qualifying scheduled event or governance-history tag.
invalidation: Bookings and backlog fail to convert into revenue, fiscal-Q3 sales or adjusted non-GAAP operating margin materially miss the disclosed outlook, or AI data-center networking demand contracts sharply.
